title: Invertibility and finite normalization of varying-ring proper/open mates
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. On a small representative of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ consist of $B_{n,W}$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and compatible componentwise morphisms. Use $D(\mathscr S_W)$ and the simultaneous geometric section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $P_u=u^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$ of $P_u\dashv R_u$, and $J_j=j_!$ for exact open extension. All maps below are actual derived-system maps with their quotient transitions.

Let $k_1:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $i:C\hookrightarrow D$ be quasi-compact open immersions, $r:A\to C$ and $p_1:B\to D$ proper, and $p_1k_1=ir$. Put $B_C=B\times_D C$, with projections $b:B_C\to B$, $q:B_C\to C$, and induced clopen immersion $s=(k_1,r):A\to B_C$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Let $\rho_s:F\to J_sP_sF$ be identity on $s(A)$ and zero on its complementary open. Let $\beta:P_{p_1}J_i\cong J_bP_q$ be the open-unit-normalized base-change map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Define
$$a_Q=(J_b\rho_sP_q)\beta:P_{p_1}J_i\longrightarrow J_{k_1}P_r,$$
using $J_bJ_s\cong J_{k_1}$, and
$$\gamma_Q=R_{p_1}(J_{k_1}\varepsilon_r)R_{p_1}(a_QR_r)\eta_{p_1}J_iR_r:J_iR_r\longrightarrow R_{p_1}J_{k_1}.$$
For every $H\in D(\mathscr S_A)$ whose levels have bounded constructible pro-etale cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], $\gamma_{Q,H}$ is an isomorphism. Under the canonical evaluation, open and direct-image comparisons, its evaluation at $n$ is exactly the proper/open comparison of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] with constant coefficient ring $B=A_n$, transported from any bounded etale-origin witness for $H_n$ [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. This identifies the specified mate and its inverse, naturally in $H$, including refinement squares $r=1$ and non-Cartesian squares. No common lower bound in $n$, normalization of $H$, finite Tor bound or flatness of $A_m\to A_n$ is required.

proof.text: For each coefficient level independently, restrict constant-ring modules to fixed modules using the proved exact equivalence fixedRestriction. Convert the given finite-stratification local constancy and finite geometric stalks to finite constant models by lem-sf-proetale-lisse-finite-models. Cohomology comparison transports constructibility and the given finite interval. The proved fixedDerivedOrigin helper in lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin supplies a bounded etale antecedent by bounded triangulated descent from the fixed-module constructible origin. Package its comparison image as the finite bounded-below object and its identity origin. The normalized cFixed comparison for identity scalars identifies the realization followed by scalar restriction with the identity on fixed modules. The derived equivalence lifts this comparison to the original constant-ring category. Thus a ScalarEtaleOrigin exists with precisely the level coefficient ring and identity scalar map. This is a proof of existence, not a data definition choosing an arbitrary origin.

Apply gamma_finite from lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting at each level and any identity-scalar origin. Its equation compares the evaluated defining mate with the specified finiteGamma, not merely an arbitrary isomorphism. All finite source, target, scalar transport and finiteGamma arrows are isomorphisms. Cancel the source and target comparison isomorphisms to deduce invertibility of evaluation of the actual system mate.

The composite of derived evaluation to a constant strict tower and its index-zero evaluation is canonically the ordinary exact derived level evaluation: use the exact-functor composition comparison and the identity constant-diagram evaluation. Apply joint detection of isomorphisms in lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections to get IsIso for the system mate. Set e to its canonical asIso. For any e-prime with the given forward mate, cancel e.hom in its naturality equation to prove the required inverse naturality.

For every origin witness, apply gamma_finite again. Expand only the source and target comparison composites, use functor preservation of composition and cancel evaluation of evalTarget.hom. Iso extensionality yields exactly the required isomorphism normalization, which also identifies inverse arrows. No interval common to different levels or additional geometric, flatness or Tor condition is used.
